sections.label: Budget debate participation figures
sections.summary: Despite COVID-19, 66 speakers debated the Budget over two and a half days, with 639 cuts filed across seven days of COS and about 130 PQs taken.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Despite this, we did not allow COVID-19 to disrupt our work: 66 speakers spoke over the two and a half days of debate on the Budget Statement; seven days COS in which 639 cuts were filed; we spent a total 73 hours debating the fiscal policy of the Government and the Ministries' Estimates of Expenditures.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Approximately 130 PQs were taken in the past two weeks.

sections.label: Transformative Budget approved
sections.summary: Parliament debated and approved a transformative Budget setting Singapore towards becoming fairer, greener, more inclusive and more progressive.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, we debated and approved one of our most transformative Budgets to date, setting ourselves on a path towards becoming a fairer, greener, more inclusive and overall, more progressive Singapore.

sections.label: Workers, wages and sustainability measures
sections.summary: Progressive Wage Model, Progressive Wage Credit Scheme and Workfare enhancements will uplift lower-wage workers, while work pass salary increases, COMPASS, carbon tax and sustainability measures are set out.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Model, Progressive Wage Credit Scheme and enhancement of the workfare income supplement scheme will support and uplift our lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We can now continue to develop a strong and skilled Singaporean workforce while enabling employers to meet genuine manpower needs by hiring foreigners with relevant skills to complement our local workforce, through the increases in the minimum qualifying salaries for work passes and the COMPASS points-based framework.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are speeding up our transition to a greener, more sustainable society with the review of our climate plan and the setting of more ambitious goals, the increase in carbon tax, R&D into sustainability, cutting emissions, energy efficiency, renewable and clean energy and zero-waste.

sections.label: Healthier SG and education reforms
sections.summary: Healthier SG provides a blueprint for preventive healthcare, and education reforms will remove mid-year exams by 2023 and streaming fully by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With Healthier SG we have the blueprint for a new model of healthcare of the future, anchored on prevention as well as cure.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have continued our educational reforms, reducing pressure and stress so our children can focus on the joy of learning – mid-year examinations for all Primary and Secondary levels will be removed by 2023 and streaming would be removed fully 2024.

sections.label: GST increase support measures
sections.summary: Most Singaporeans will not feel the GST increase for years because support measures and GSTV keep lower income, including retirees, paying less than the headline rate.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Most Singaporeans will not feel the impact of the GST increase for many years because of the support measures we designed.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: By coupling GST with GSTV, we ensure that the lower income, including many retirees, will continue to pay less GST than the headline rate.

sections.label: GST and assistance schemes
sections.summary: Government structures are fair and progressive, with GST offset for low-income by the Permanent GST Voucher scheme, and the Assurance Package helping all households with the transition.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On the Government side, the structures that we have put in place are ones we believe are fair and progressive.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: There is GST; yes, but will not hurt the low-income because of Permanent GST Voucher scheme, and the Assurance Package will help all Singaporean households, not just the lower-income cope with the transition, and the GST Voucher scheme provides permanent assistance.

sections.label: Taxing large companies and rich
sections.summary: Proposals to raise $3.5 billion yearly would tax large companies and the rich more or use more reserves, but adjusting corporate taxes is premature pending BEPS 2.0 rules.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To achieve additional revenue of $3.5 billion a year, the net effect of their various proposals is to tax large companies more, tax the rich or use more of the reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: From our perspective, it is too early to adjust corporate taxes as it will depend on the evolving rules for BEPS 2.0.

sections.label: Mobility of wealth and taxes
sections.summary: Wealth is mobile, so higher taxes on a small, extremely mobile top group will eventually lead to higher taxes for upper middle-income or middle-income groups.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In reality, wealth is mobile, higher taxes on a small group of people at the top who are extremely mobile will eventually lead to higher taxes for upper middle-income or even middle-income groups.

sections.label: Ukraine invasion and inflation impact
sections.summary: Amid the pandemic's economic effects, the Russian invasion of Ukraine is felt through rising petrol prices, and suspending Russian oil and gas purchases could affect energy prices and cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Even as we deal with the economic ramifications of this pandemic that has stricken every nation on earth and affected everyone, we are now caught in the grips of the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It may seem remote, but we are all feeling the impact immediately, with petrol prices going up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Inflation was a worry even before this conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: If the West were to suspend purchase of Russian oil and gas, what would that impact be on energy prices and on cost of living?

sections.label: US-China tensions and ageing
sections.summary: Concerns include geopolitical implications of the US-China clash and Singapore's demographic trend that by 2030 one in four will be 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We are concerned about the geopolitical implications of the clash between the US and China, and how we are caught up in between them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We are worried about demographic trends in Singapore – by 2030, one in four of us will be 65 and above.

sections.label: Addressing present and future concerns
sections.summary: The key thing is whether we can address concerns for the present and future, and whether we have the means and ability to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The key thing is how are we able to address the concerns, both for the present and to stage ourselves for the future; and if we have the means and the ability to do that.

sections.label: Reasons flats are not upkept
sections.summary: Those involved in the work know flats are sometimes not upkept because of mental health issues, hoarding, or mobility issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: For those of us involved in the work, you will know that sometimes, it is because of mental health issues, because of hoarding; sometimes, because of mobility issues – the individuals are not able to upkeep the flats.

sections.label: Global divisions and polarisation
sections.summary: The passage states that global divisions and polarisation have real implications, citing American society, Capitol Hill and BREXIT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: When we look at the combination of these different things in the world that we are living in today, it has real implications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We see around the world today, for example, the divisions and the polarisation of American society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And I believe that even the storming of Capitol Hill is arguably a physical and violent manifestation of that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: BREXIT also happened on the back of a number of fraudulent claims by political leaders.

sections.label: Race and religion politics
sections.summary: The passage states that race and religion is an easy game to play because it is primordial in every society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Race and religion is an easy game to play because it is so primordial in every society.

sections.label: Trust and respect leadership
sections.summary: The passage asks whether we rise above it and take a different course, stating we lead only because there is trust and respect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Or do we rise above it and take a different course?

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We lead only because there is trust and respect.

sections.label: Singapore public housing policies
sections.summary: The passage states 80% of Singaporeans live in public housing, 73% service loans with CPF, and cites rental blocks and home ownership figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: As we are talking about the different things to improve on, many of our foreign visitors, as you talk to them, are remarkably impressed about our public housing policies: 80 % of Singaporeans live in public housing; 73% – like many of my residents, they are not high-income Singaporeans, they are middle-, lower-middle Singaporeans – 73% of them service their loans with CPF, with no cash outlay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: For low-income families, I have a number of rental blocks as well, we have, in total, about 4,500 families in the last five years who have gained home ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And another 2,200 who have booked their new flats.

sections.label: Employment and unemployment rates
sections.summary: The passage states the employment rate for those aged 15 and above was 67.2% in June 2021 and the unemployment rate was 3.1% in January.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Our employment rate for those aged 15 and above, is 67.2% in June 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In January, our unemployment rate is 3.1%, and it is close to back where it was pre-COVID-19 times.

sections.label: President's Challenge 2019 funds
sections.summary: The passage states that President's Challenge, for example, in 2019, raised $13.2 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: President’s Challenge, for example, in 2019, raised $13.2 million.

sections.label: Building on foundations for Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states that foundations have been laid, Bills passed, and that the House must now execute, improve and build on them to make a difference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Are we able to make things better for Singapore, for today and for tomorrow?

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I believe that we have laid the foundations for this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And I am grateful to all who have contributed to that on both sides of the House to debate the issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It now leaves for us, as we have passed all the necessary Bills and so on, to execute it and to make it happen, to improve on it, and to build on it, so that we come back again next year and repeat the process, so that we can make the difference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Of all the countries in the world, as we are all struggling with all the challenges that we face, I think we can be confident that we have the wherewithal to look after our people.
